answer_1.quote: The goal is to reframe such arguments to be more trustworthy (e.g., less partisan, no appeal to fear fallacy), while maintaining the same denotative meaning of the input argument. We introduce our approach called ENTRUST : ArgumENT Reframing with langUage modelS and enTailment
datasets: Appeal to Fear or Prejudice dataset

answer_2.quote: Automatic evaluation. ... To this end we calculate Semantic Similarity with our input using SENTENCE BERT(SBERT).

answer_4.quote: Human evaluation. We use Amazon Mechanical Turk to evaluate on a total of 900 utterances ... We proposed a set of 3 criteria to evaluate the generated output: (1) Fluency ... (2) Meaning Preservation ... (3) Trustworthiness/Presence of Fear
answer_4.guideline: Turkers were asked to rate reframed arguments based on fluency, meaning preservation, trustworthiness (for partisan arguments), and presence of fear (for appeal to fear fallacies)
